chunks: And ʿAlī ibn Jaʿfar asked his brother Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar, peace be upon them:
About a man who prays while there is something from the birds in front of him, he said: “There is no harm.”

And about a man who prays while a date-palm is in front of him and it has its fruit, he said: “There is no harm.” And about a man who prays in a vineyard while it has its fruit, he said: “There is no harm.”

And about a man who prays while a donkey is standing in front of him, he said: “He should place between himself and it a reed, or a stick, or something that he sets up between them, then he may pray, and there is no harm.”

And about a man who prays while he has with him a pouch made from the hide of a donkey or mule, he said: “It is not proper that he pray while it is with him, unless he fears its loss; then there is no harm in praying while it is with him.”

And about a man whose tooth becomes loose while he is in salat (prayer), whether he should remove it, he said: “If it does not make him bleed, then let him remove it; and if it causes bleeding, then let him leave.”
And about a man who prays while there is a bird in his sleeve, he said: “If he fears its escaping, then there is no harm.”

And about a man who has a wart or a wound, whether it is proper for him to cut the wart while he is in his salat (prayer), or pluck some of his flesh from that wound and cast it away, he said: “If he does not fear that blood will flow, then there is no harm; but if he fears that blood will flow, then he should not do it.”

And about a man who is in his salat (prayer), then another man strikes him and wounds his head so that blood flows, so he leaves and washes it, and he does not speak until he returns to the mosque, whether he may count what he has prayed or begin the salat (prayer) anew, he said: “He begins the salat (prayer) anew and does not count anything of what he had prayed.”
And about a man who sees on his garment bird droppings or something else, whether he may scrape it off while he is in his salat (prayer), he said: “There is no harm.”
And he said: “There is no harm in a man raising his gaze toward the sky while he is praying.”

key_terms.الدَّمُ: blood whose flowing affects the ruling of prayer
key_terms.النَّخْلَةُ: a date-palm tree standing before the worshipper
key_terms.حِمَارٌ: a donkey standing in front of the person praying
key_terms.دَبَّةٌ: a pouch or container carried by the person
key_terms.قَصَبَةً: a reed or similar object used as a barrier

ai.seo_question: What things in front of or with a person during salat (prayer) affect the validity of the prayer according to Imam Mūsā ibn Jaʿfar عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gathers several legal rulings related to salat (prayer), especially concerning things present before the worshipper, objects carried during prayer, minor bodily actions, bleeding, and interruption of the prayer. It shows what does not invalidate prayer, what is disliked or improper, and when bleeding or leaving the prayer requires beginning the salat (prayer) again.
